periodFactors._note: ASSUMPTION: hourly volume relative to the PM peak hour on arterials; typical urban weekday profile, to be calibrated.

kFactorNote: ASSUMPTION: peak-hour share of ADT for urban arterials (typically 0.08-0.10); not derived from local data.

classDefaultAdt._note: ASSUMPTION: per-class default two-way ADT when no count exists for the gate street. Documented values; a class with at least classDefaultFromCounts.minStreets counted streets takes their median instead (DATA-derived, see the build log); uncalibrated otherwise.

classDefaultFromCounts._decision: Switched off on 2026-11-12 (minStreets set out of reach). Counted streets are the busiest of their class, so their median overstates uncounted gates: it raised tertiary from 5,000 to 12,200 ADT and made the baseline less stable (150 vs 88 vehicles removed per PM hour).
classDefaultFromCounts._note: DATA: the default ADT of a gate class is the median ADT of the counted streets of that class in this data set (a TMC leg's peak-hour entering plus leaving volume over K, or a Caltrans station ADT times its factor; one value per street) when at least `minStreets` such streets exist; otherwise the documented value above stays. Counted streets are the busiest of their class, so the median is a high estimate for the uncounted gates.

streetCounts._note: DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour turning-movement counts at Telegraph Ave & Alcatraz Ave (Quality Counts; 2018-09-11, 2018-09-12, 2019-09-10, 2021-09-29), averaged. Leg volumes entering/leaving the intersection are used for gates lying on that leg's street in that compass direction from the count intersection (N/E/S/W). A gate takes the leg of the nearest counted intersection on its street and compass direction (within maxLegDistM), so gates far from this intersection use it as a proxy.

DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour turning-movement counts at Telegraph Ave & 40th St (Quality Counts; 2018-09-11, 2018-09-12, 2019-09-10, 2021-09-29), averaged. Intersection lies ~90 m south of the model edge; the north leg serves the Telegraph Ave gate on the south edge.
DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour counts at West St & 40th St (same four count dates), averaged. Serves the West St and 40th St gates on the south edge.
DATA: Oakland PM peak-hour counts at Market St & 55th St (same four count dates), averaged. Serves the Market St and 55th St gates.

adtOverrides.source: SR-13 at Claremont Ave, Berkeley PM 10.79, ahead AADT 23,500 (back 32,500); the Claremont/College gate lies ~1 km away, so ASSUMPTION factor 0.6 attenuation.
SR-13 Ashby Ave at the SR-123 junction (San Pablo Ave), Berkeley PM 13.178, back AADT 28,000 (east side; ahead 43,500): applies to the Ashby Ave gate at the west edge (Caltrans 2023-24 count year).
SR-13 at Domingo Ave, Berkeley PM 10.69, back AADT 27,000 (east side; ahead 32,500): applies to the Tunnel Road gate east of the SR-24/SR-13 ramps (Caltrans 2023-24 count year).
SR-123 San Pablo Ave at JCT RTE 13, Berkeley PM 1.906, back AADT 21,700 (ahead 22,800).
SR-123 San Pablo Ave at Stanford Ave, Oakland PM 1.12, AADT 21,300 back / 19,700 ahead (mean 20,500).

streetMatch._note: Lower-case substrings of OSM link names mapped to a count key.

gravity.balanceNote: Through-trip balancing: counted gates keep their outflow target and the assumed gates are scaled to the inflow supply (before, every gate was scaled to 0.77 of its target).

local._note: ASSUMPTION: vehicle trip rates per resident worker / per job per weekday; ITE-like order of magnitude, uncalibrated.
local.vehicleModeShareNote: ASSUMPTION: drive-alone+carpool share for commutes (ACS-like; not derived here).

freewayNote: Links of these classes form the freeway. Gates on them are freeway gates: they only exchange trips with surface streets through the ramps found in the network (surface nodes touched by both freeway and surface links). Freeway mainline-to-mainline trips are not generated (they never touch surface streets).

ramps._note: Ramp demand. DATA: ramp ADT rows from Caltrans ramp-volume workbooks (raw.caltransRamps), matched to network ramps by street name (streetMatch) and type (OFF TO / ON FR); latest count year used, no growth applied (ASSUMPTION). Everything below is ASSUMPTION unless stated.
ramps.kFactorNote: ASSUMPTION: peak-hour share of ramp ADT, same urban range as the arterial K-factor; period volume factors (periodFactors) apply on top.
ramps.defaultAdtNote: ASSUMPTION: ADT of a ramp with no matching published count (minor connectors at the SR-13/SR-24 interchange, hillside ramps and the Broadway terminals east of Tunnel Road). The original four ramps never used it.
ramps.localShareNote: ASSUMPTION (calibration step V: 0.30 -> 0.60, tested 0.30 / 0.45 / 0.60 / 0.75): share of ramp trips whose surface end is an in-area (LODES) node rather than a surface gate. The model area is 5.7 by 3.4 km, so most ramp trips end inside it. These trips replace part of the block's external local trips.
ramps.maxShareOfGateNote: ASSUMPTION: ramp trips use at most this share of a surface gate's in/outflow target (surface totals stay consistent; the Furness step fills the rest).

destination._note: ASSUMPTION: gravity over surface gates and local nodes, attraction x direction plausibility. Plausibility = exp(-(dTheta/sigma)^2) floored, where dTheta is the angle between the bearing ramp->destination and the bearing ramp->study-area center. No distance term. Street choice is left to the simulator.
destination.poolingNote: Surface ends of ramp trips are drawn per ramp ('ramp') instead of once per mainline gate over every ramp the gate reaches ('gate'): ramps far apart that feed one gate (Claremont/Hudson and Miles on the WB gate, the Caldecott and Broadway Terrace ramps) were pooled, so trips from the whole west side were sent to the Claremont on-ramp. Each ramp keeps its own DATA volume, bearing and access time.
destination.accessTauS_note: ASSUMPTION: access decay of a ramp trip's surface end, exp(-t / accessTauS) with t the router's generalized cost in seconds from the surface end to the ramp (to it for an on-ramp, from it for an off-ramp). 150, 300 and 600 s were tried (baseline-calibration record, eighth round); 0 turns it off.

ramps.aliasNote: ASSUMPTION: the Caltrans descriptions (EB OFF TO BROADWAY, WB OFF TO COLLEGE AVE, ...) are matched to ramp terminals by location, from OSM destination tags and postmile order, because the surface street names at the terminals (Keith Ave, Miles Ave, Brookside Ave, Broadway) differ. Verify against Caltrans ramp maps before relying on them.
ramps.excludeNote: Rows that combine the 52nd St and MLK Jr Way (Grove St) ramps are dropped because per-street SEG rows (2016-2017 / 2012) exist for the same ramps and would double count.

active._note: ASSUMPTION unless stated: walking and biking demand (design D6). Person trips use the car model's per-worker and per-job rates (local.*), then these mode shares. Volumes are persons per hour. Only the count scaling below uses data (DATA: Oakland pedestrian and bicycle counts at one intersection); everything else is uncounted. ACS commute mode shares were not retrievable (the Census API needs a key), so the shares are not derived from them.

pedestrian.modeShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of person trips made on foot; the observed count scaling overrides the absolute level.
pedestrian.meanTripNote: ASSUMPTION: mean of the exponential trip-length decay (network meters).
pedestrian.maxTripNote: ASSUMPTION: longest walk to another in-area node.
pedestrian.commercialShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of in-area walking trips ending on a primary or secondary street inside the study area (shops, services).
pedestrian.gateShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of walking trips leaving or entering the model at a gate.
pedestrian.gateMaxNote: ASSUMPTION: gates beyond this network distance get no walking trips.
pedestrian.periodVolumeNote: ASSUMPTION: hourly volume relative to the PM peak (the scaling period).

bicycle.modeShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of person trips made by bicycle; the observed count scaling overrides the absolute level.
bicycle.meanTripNote: ASSUMPTION: mean of the exponential trip-length decay (network meters).
bicycle.gateShareNote: ASSUMPTION: share of cycling trips leaving or entering the model at a gate.
bicycle.throughNote: ASSUMPTION: gate-to-gate bicycle trips as a share of all trips starting at in-area nodes.
bicycle.routeBonusNote: ASSUMPTION: gate pairs whose shortest bike path runs along bike lanes and routes get up to 1 + routeBonus times the weight.
bicycle.laneRouteCostNote: ASSUMPTION: bike-path cost of a link with a bike lane (routes use the midpoint to 1); only steers which shortest path counts as the cyclist's.
bicycle.periodVolumeNote: ASSUMPTION: hourly volume relative to the PM peak (the scaling period).

countScaling._note: DATA: one factor per mode makes PM peak-hour persons passing the counted intersection (shortest paths, ends included) equal the mean of the Oakland counts (config streetCounts[0]), measured on the final flow list after the flow cap; the factor is not clamped and applies to all periods and places. A factor far from 1 means the assumed mode share and trip rates are off by that factor.

active.maxFlowsNote: Keeps all modes together under about 12,000 flows per period (cars are capped at maxFlows above, 8,000).

peripheral._note: ASSUMPTION: gate-to-gate trips that never come within nearM of the study area are kept as background load. P1: pairs whose gates are less than minPerimeterGapM apart along the model-area perimeter, or whose free-flow route stays within edgeBandM of the model edge, are corner-clipping and are not generated (their volume goes to other pairs at the same gates, so counted gates keep their counts). P2: a gate's modeled volume may not exceed min(its target, its lane capacity x cordon.signalizedVehPerHourPerLane); the excess is taken from that gate's peripheral through trips only. Ramp volumes and counted volumes are never reduced.

cordon._note: Measured capacities of the validation suite (data/calibration/validation.md): a signalized lane at green share 0.5 (cases b1, b2) and a motorway lane at 65 mph (case i1).

countFit._note: Count-constrained demand (seventh round). Every count the pipeline holds is a target volume on directed links; OD flows are scaled so that a free-flow static assignment matches them. Citation for the method family: [VanZuylen1980], [Willumsen1981]. Targets for AM and midday are the PM counts scaled by periodFactors (ASSUMPTION).

bounds._note: ASSUMPTION: limits on a flow's cumulative factor.

countFit.drawsNote: ASSUMPTION: each flow is split equally over this many free-flow shortest paths found with link costs perturbed by +/- noise (the simulator's perceived-cost noise is also 8%); 1 draw and 0 noise gives all-or-nothing assignment.

uncounted._note: ASSUMPTION: a flow that passes no counted link takes the volume-weighted median factor of the counted flows of its type (through, local, ramp); alternatives: medianAll, one.

weights._note: Weights of the constraint families in the geometric mean over the counted links of a flow's paths.

capacityGuard._note: ASSUMPTION-labeled sanity guard, not data: an uncounted link may carry at most capacity x (1 + excessShare); flows above are scaled down proportionally. Capacities are the simulator's own measured values from data/calibration/validation.md (cases named in each entry), per lane or per approach by the control at the link's end node. Counted links are exempt.

two_way_stop_minor.source: validation e4 (minor through, major 200 per direction)

two_way_stop_major.source: validation g1 (free single lane at 25 mph)

motorway_signal.source: validation i2 (off-ramp terminal at a signal)

countFit.convergenceNote: Stopping rule of the fit: every count station outside tolerance is either blocked (the flows it needs to move sit on a bound, share >= blockedShare) or in tension (another station outside tolerance the other way shares at least half of its flow, or the capacity guard pulls most of its flow down), and the volume-weighted mean relative step of the flows is below softStep; otherwise stop as stalled (worst log error of the other stations improved by less than stallGain over stallWindow iterations), or when no flow moves by more than `stationary`. Blocked and tense stations are listed in the fit report with what holds them back.

assignment._note: method 'free': the free-flow assignment over `draws` perturbed shortest paths (draws and noise above). Method 'msa': stochastic capacity-restrained assignment: each pass loads every flow with `drawsPerPass` driver walks (the simulator's rule: cost-to-go with a +/-noise factor per candidate link) over link costs x BPR(volume / capacity), volumes averaged over passes (method of successive averages [PowellSheffi1982]); BPR form [Spiess1990] with alpha 0.15 and beta 4 (ASSUMPTION: the usual values); capacities from capacityGuard.capacity; `rounds` > 1 refits the table and reassigns at its own volumes.

shares._note: Observed route shares (StreetLight select-link and ramp via-street shares) as ratio constraints in the same fit, weight below the counts' (1 to 2) because the shares come from a device sample (ASSUMPTION: 0.5). 0 or enabled false leaves them out.
